title: Underneath the Crooked Moon
summary: The Crooked Tree burned, the moon scowls, and the train comes out of the fog.

epilogue.title: The Queen in the Moon
epilogue.text: Kehlenn is bound and scowling, and she will be for ever. But a split soul was let go unmended, and the old folk say a new Horned King comes in twenty years.

epilogue.title: The Queen in the Moon
epilogue.text: The Crooked Moon's grin has turned to a scowl, and it stays that way. Kehlenn watches the valley from the sky and cannot reach it.

epilogue.title: The Lord and Lady
epilogue.text: Phillip and Adela Druskenvald are gone, embracing in the ash of the tree. Somebody among you keeps a small keepsake of theirs, and does not speak of it.

epilogue.title: Wickermoor
epilogue.text: Wickermoor was rebuilt from its own ash, plank by plank, by people who had run and then come back.

epilogue.title: Wickermoor
epilogue.text: There is barely a village left: a few lit windows round the Round, and more stones in the ground than doors on the street.

epilogue.title: Wickermoor
epilogue.text: Wickermoor is a quiet town now, quiet at the hours it used to sing. The Round is swept every dawn all the same.

epilogue.title: Wickermoor
epilogue.text: Wickermoor is scarred but whole. The oak is still carved with faces, the neighbours are still unkind about each other's pies, and nobody minds.

epilogue.title: The Ones Who Came Back
epilogue.text: The neighbours who were chained at the stones walk the Round again. They do not say thank you aloud, but pies appear on the heroes' doorstep.

epilogue.title: The Ones Who Came Back
epilogue.text: Those pulled from the stones are alive, which is a heavy thing to be. They stand at the graves of the ones who were not, and they stand there a long time.

epilogue.title: The Green Queen Inn
epilogue.text: Marianna Grey keeps the inn under a will most of the village is still arguing over. She keeps the stable, too, and the horses prefer her.

epilogue.title: The Green Queen Inn
epilogue.text: The Green Queen Inn is boarded up. The nights of bedlam left it with its shutters nailed and its sign facing the wall.

epilogue.title: The Green Queen Inn
epilogue.text: The mourners keep the inn's bar open, taking turns behind it, and nobody has settled on whose name goes over the door.

epilogue.title: The Mayor and the Watch
epilogue.text: Mayor Somerton lived, and was thanked for it, which he found much harder to bear than being blamed.

epilogue.title: The Mayor and the Watch
epilogue.text: The mob took Mayor Somerton before anyone could find the right form to stop it. The village has not forgiven itself, which he would have found very correct.

epilogue.title: The Mayor and the Watch
epilogue.text: Mayor Somerton sits in his own cells, writing an immense petition to himself. Doris Squire brings him tea and does not read it.

epilogue.title: The Mayor and the Watch
epilogue.text: Doris Squire rebuilds the watch alone, from a roster with one name on it. She writes in the margins when no one is looking.

epilogue.title: The Old Ways
epilogue.text: The burned Wytchwood grows green again, and the faithful read it as the Green Queen's return. They are not entirely wrong, and nobody tells them so.

epilogue.title: The Old Ways
epilogue.text: The faithful who were never corrupted harden. They blame outsiders, bar their doors, and drive off other groups who come asking.

epilogue.title: The Patient Lady's Fold
epilogue.text: The Patient Lady's fold cast out their own magic-users and walk into the wilds unprepared. Sister Rain goes with them, counting heads and humming.

epilogue.title: The Brightsingers
epilogue.text: Many of the Brightsingers rose in light with the rapture, and the chapel Weston built is mostly songbooks now.

epilogue.title: The Brightsingers
epilogue.text: Emboldened, the Brightsingers call for more missionaries and convert hard. The songs are louder and no less cheerful.

epilogue.title: The Newcomers
epilogue.text: Eleanor, Finneas and Jean climb aboard behind you with their trunks, and the Express carries them as far as they care to go.

epilogue.title: The Newcomers
epilogue.text: The newcomers pack their trunks and leave the valley, some of them on the Ghostlight Express, none of them sorry.

epilogue.title: Foxwillow
epilogue.text: Foxwillow's crows were freed from the fields and the town is rebuilding in the open, shamed, with its eyes up.

epilogue.title: Foxwillow
epilogue.text: Foxwillow keeps its crows, and sings to them each dusk. A one-legged stranger named Virgil unites the town under a god of the four winds.

epilogue.title: Foxwillow
epilogue.text: Foxwillow keeps its crows too close. Shame and distrust sit at every table, and the Patient Lady is abandoned for a god of the four winds.

epilogue.title: The Foxwillow Fields
epilogue.text: The farmers of Foxwillow heard the truth of the fields, and Jeremiah Stover was paid fairly for the telling.

epilogue.title: The Foxwillow Fields
epilogue.text: The lie told about the fields held. It sits badly in the soil, and every harvest tastes faintly of it.

epilogue.title: The Foxwillow Fields
epilogue.text: The fields were never explained, and the silence took root. The crop is poor and the soil is kind.

epilogue.title: Dawn's Gate
epilogue.text: Dawn's Gate learned who the Crimson Rose really was, and its faith broke in the open. Riders hunt the missionaries who stayed to argue.

epilogue.title: Dawn's Gate
epilogue.text: Without its hidden hand the power vacuum shows Viraxys anyway, and Dawn's Gate's faith collapses. All worship is outlawed and riders hunt missionaries.

epilogue.title: Murkwater Bend
epilogue.text: Snake Eye Magnolias bloom in the Drowned Crossroads, a boom follows, and Vander Boone courts the Crescent Court to make the Hollow a province.

epilogue.title: Skitterdeep
epilogue.text: Skitterdeep Mine is quiet, its thirteen made safe the hard way, and the diggers do not speak of the kennel.

epilogue.title: Skitterdeep
epilogue.text: The diggers of Skitterdeep took the mine back and keep a watch on the lower galleries that never sleeps.

epilogue.title: Skitterdeep
epilogue.text: Skitterdeep Mine keeps its thirteen secrets. The sick of the village no longer come from its mouth, which is something.

epilogue.title: Hartsblight
epilogue.text: The garden in Hartsblight is tended, and what grows there is only a garden. The commune goat eats a share of it.

epilogue.title: Hartsblight
epilogue.text: The garden in Hartsblight burned, and the forest around it has not forgiven the smoke.

epilogue.title: Hartsblight
epilogue.text: Hartsblight's garden was moved, and moves again on quiet nights. The commune goat has stopped being surprised.

epilogue.title: Maidenmist
epilogue.text: Isolde still walks Maidenmist's lanes, and the cemetery has learned to keep her company.

epilogue.title: Maidenmist
epilogue.text: Maidenmist lays its dead to rest in order, with epitaphs argued over by committee, which is the village's idea of peace.

epilogue.title: The Festival of Fools
epilogue.text: The Festival of Fools remembers the day its king was exposed, and has made a holiday of it, with a very small crown.

epilogue.title: The Festival of Fools
epilogue.text: The Festival of Fools ended in a wedding after all, and the guests are still arguing over the seating.

epilogue.title: The Festival of Fools
epilogue.text: The Festival of Fools packed up in the night, leaving bunting in the trees and a lingering sense of being laughed at.

epilogue.title: The Roving Rookery
epilogue.text: The Rookery's posse was talked down, and the roosts moved on with their feathers in better order.

epilogue.title: The Roving Rookery
epilogue.text: The Roving Rookery rolls on, wherever the wind lets it, and the roosts are harder to find every year.

epilogue.title: The Jenkin Family
epilogue.text: The Jenkin family went back to the crooked house to put it in order. It takes some of them an afternoon to find the front door.

epilogue.title: The Founders' Feast
epilogue.text: Holly Aster's spiced loaf won the Founders' feast. It is still remembered, and the recipe was found in her apron.

epilogue.title: The Founders' Feast
epilogue.text: Siv Harga's sausage rolls won the Founders' feast, and she shares the recipe with no one, which is her way of grieving.

epilogue.title: The Founders' Feast
epilogue.text: The Founders' feast served both Holly's loaf and Siv's rolls at one table, and the village still talks about how good the dinner was.

epilogue.title: The Fair Price
epilogue.text: The book trade settled in Eleanor Heyling's favour. She cites the settlement in footnotes to this day.

epilogue.title: The Fair Price
epilogue.text: The Trading Post kept its prices, and Baltus Tolliver's last receipt is framed above the empty counter.

epilogue.title: The Fair Price
epilogue.text: The Trading Post and its rivals kept a truce on prices, and shopping in Wickermoor became briefly civil.

epilogue.title: Mori Shade
epilogue.text: Mori Shade burned what you entrusted to her, and she scatters the ash on new graves.

epilogue.title: Mori Shade
epilogue.text: Mori took her secret to Doris Squire, and the two of them keep a ledger of the dead between them.

epilogue.title: Mori Shade
epilogue.text: Mori heeded your warning, and every grave she dug had its name written twice.

epilogue.title: Mori Shade
epilogue.text: Mori kept her silence, and the village is the quieter for it.

epilogue.title: Mrs. Oakum
epilogue.text: Mrs. Oakum was helped through her long nights, and the butcher's shop opens early again.

epilogue.title: Mrs. Oakum
epilogue.text: Mrs. Oakum's secret was told, and she keeps to the hills, leaving meat scraps on the wall.

epilogue.title: Mrs. Oakum
epilogue.text: Mrs. Oakum's secret was kept, and she sleeps on the butcher's floor with the door barred, in peace.

epilogue.title: Thomasin's Curses
epilogue.text: Thomasin Ardor unpicked the old curses stitch by stitch, and made the heroes coats from what was left.

epilogue.title: Thomasin's Curses
epilogue.text: An apology was made and taken, and Thomasin Ardor opens the shop earlier, with the door wide.

epilogue.title: Thomasin's Curses
epilogue.text: The truth about the curses came out, and it hurt, and it mended something that had been wrong a long time.

epilogue.title: Thomasin's Curses
epilogue.text: The warning about the curses was heeded, and the tailor's window is full of fanciful clothes at last.

epilogue.title: Barnaby Pennywhistle
epilogue.text: Barnaby Pennywhistle was exposed and run out of the valley, and his cure is still sold by a cousin.

epilogue.title: Barnaby Pennywhistle
epilogue.text: Morgan went into business with Barnaby Pennywhistle, to everyone's regret, and the cure is now guaranteed in writing.

epilogue.title: Barnaby Pennywhistle
epilogue.text: Barnaby Pennywhistle was let go, and he still sells his cure at the edge of the valley, with a new guarantee.

epilogue.title: The Quarantine
epilogue.text: A forged quarantine order saved the village from one sickness and gave it another: a suspicion of all paperwork.

epilogue.title: The Letter
epilogue.text: The letter you carried reached its reader, and Geneva Fairchild still keeps the receipt.

epilogue.title: The Letter
epilogue.text: The letter was seized, and never answered. Geneva Fairchild runs the post alone and checks every seal twice.

epilogue.title: The Monastery Bell
epilogue.text: The bell of the Crimson Monastery rings again, and the whole valley hears it at the turn of the hour.

epilogue.title: The Monastery Bell
epilogue.text: The monastery bell stayed silent, and the Brightsingers fill the gap with singing.

epilogue.title: The Conductor's Punch
epilogue.text: The conductor's understudy kept the punch, and now insists on being called the conductor on all the Express's paperwork.

epilogue.title: The Conductor's Punch
epilogue.text: The party kept the conductor's punch, and the Vagrant has never once mentioned it.

epilogue.title: The Conductor's Punch
epilogue.text: The conductor's punch went into a chair's stuffing and is probably still there, mending tickets in its sleep.

epilogue.title: The Lounge Car
epilogue.text: The Express's lounge car was seated in peace, and the ghosts still talk of it.

epilogue.title: The Lounge Car
epilogue.text: The lounge car was seated loudly, and the ghosts still talk of it, louder.

epilogue.title: Golub Graygullet
epilogue.text: Golub Graygullet is gone and his charm is broken. The Hollow is calmer, and a few people find that harder than the fear.

epilogue.title: Chuckles
epilogue.text: Chuckles the clown is dead, and the Magician's card paid out. Somebody laid a red nose on the grave.

epilogue.title: The Wicker Man
epilogue.text: The Wicker Man's ashes are in the rafters of the new Brightsinger chapel, where they sing along.

epilogue.title: The Goat's Offer
epilogue.text: Those who took the goat's bargain carry the wish and the curse, and each knows which one is heavier on a given night.

epilogue.title: What Was Given
epilogue.text: Some of you gave your lives at the skull. Their embers rose with Adela's, and the village keeps their names on the stones by the Round.

epilogue.title: What Was Given
epilogue.text: Each of you gave something of great value at the goat skull, an heirloom, a strength, a gift. None of it came back, and none of you asked.

epilogue.title: Apocalypse
epilogue.text: A hero remembered being a time traveller, and left in a flash of light to make a gentler timeline.

epilogue.title: Apocalypse
epilogue.text: A hero remembered what they were and chose to stay, and uses the power beyond the Hollow with a careful hand.

epilogue.title: Ascendancy
epilogue.text: A hero was crowned an otherworldly monarch in a crown of ash and horn, and left everyone behind.

epilogue.title: Ascendancy
epilogue.text: A hero set the crown on their fool instead, and has been proud of the choice since, especially at breakfast.

epilogue.title: Deliverance
epilogue.text: A hero took up the ferryman's pole and left into the mist, carrying the dead where they wished to go.

epilogue.title: Deliverance
epilogue.text: A hero stayed among the living, and goes to help lost souls elsewhere, when they have time.

epilogue.title: Duality
epilogue.text: Two halves of a soul fused and were changed for ever. The hero knows themselves now, and others notice.

epilogue.title: Duality
epilogue.text: A hero let the duplicate go, and the sins they carried go with it. They will return.

epilogue.title: Evolution
epilogue.text: A hero became wholly stardust, and the glittering dust spreads through the Hollow on the wind.

epilogue.title: Evolution
epilogue.text: A hero works the stardust change on a small scale elsewhere, and keeps a jar of it on the shelf.

epilogue.title: Immortality
epilogue.text: A hero bought true immortality with a thousand souls, and the price is spoken of only in the dark.

epilogue.title: Immortality
epilogue.text: A hero made a single cure, and the souls went free. The cure works, and the hero counts the cost.

epilogue.title: Kindred
epilogue.text: A hero took their kin's place as a crooked spirit bound to Druskenvald, with their free will whole.

epilogue.title: Kindred
epilogue.text: A hero let their kin be taken, and swore to oppose them later. The oath is not forgotten.

epilogue.title: Liberation
epilogue.text: A hero won the game against the soul-owner, and the deal dissolved. The shadow that watched has become a person.

epilogue.title: Liberation
epilogue.text: A hero destroyed the soul-owner with a blade rather than a hand of cards. The cards are kept in a drawer.

epilogue.title: Malediction
epilogue.text: A hero broke the curse with the tree's ashes and blinked away beyond the stars.

epilogue.title: Malediction
epilogue.text: A hero stayed, with the incantation unspoken, and the curse is a quieter thing now.

epilogue.title: Pilgrimage
epilogue.text: A hero raised the third monument, and twisted souls were reborn as the thirteen reborn species.

epilogue.title: Pilgrimage
epilogue.text: A hero let the twisted souls fade in peace, and keeps their names on a list.

epilogue.title: Rapture
epilogue.text: A hero led the rapture, rising in light with the believing, and the sky kept a little of the glow.

epilogue.title: Rapture
epilogue.text: A hero left the god's gathering to the intervention alone, and stayed to see what grew.

epilogue.title: Rejuvenation
epilogue.text: A hero spread the embers, and the Wytchwood burned into new life in their favourite season.

epilogue.title: Rejuvenation
epilogue.text: A hero saw a vision of sick lands beyond the valley, and sets out to heal them in time.

epilogue.title: Slaughter
epilogue.text: A hero merged into an apex predator of the wilds and went hunting, and the wilds are quieter around them.

epilogue.title: Slaughter
epilogue.text: A hero hunts elsewhere, in the hills past the valley, and sends the odd pelt home.

epilogue.title: The Last Ride
epilogue.text: The Ghostlight Express carried you home, to the land of the living, with a sprig of wheat left on the seat.

epilogue.title: The Last Ride
epilogue.text: The Ghostlight Express carried you into another province of the land of eternal night, where the moon is a different shape.

epilogue.title: The Last Ride
epilogue.text: The Ghostlight Express carried you out beyond the Shroud, to a world nobody had a name for yet.

epilogue.title: The Last Ride
epilogue.text: The Ghostlight Express went on without a word, its lamp growing small in the fog.
